paragraphs.text:
The greening of planes, trains and automobiles

Moving goods and people around the world is responsible for a large part of global CO2 emissions (排放). As the world races to decarbonize everything, it faces particular problems with transportation — which accounts for about a quarter of our energy-related greenhouse gas emissions. Here’s the breakdown of the emissions in 2018 for different modes of transport.

ROAD VEHICLES
ROAD (PASSENGER) 45.1%
ROAD (GOODS) 29.4%
AIRPLANES 11.6%
SHIPPING 10.6%
RAIL 1%
OTHER 2.2%

The fuels for transport need to be not just green, cheap and powerful, but also lightweight and safe enough to be carried around. Each mode of transport has its specific fuel needs. Much is still to be settled, but here are some of the solutions to get us going green. PLANES — Synthetic hydrocarbons. The hardest sector to decarbonize is aviation. One long-term option for sustainable fuel for planes is to make hydrocarbons from recycled air. CARS — Batteries. Batteries are energy-efficient and electric cars can plug into existing systems and services. New solid-state batteries will take a car farther on a single charge. TRAINS — Electricity. Some trains are already electrified through rails or wires; others can be made electric in pretty simple ways. TRUCKS — Hydrogen fuel cells. Hydrogen fuel cells are a lighter choice than batteries for trucks, but making green hydrogen is expensive. SHIPS — Liquid ammonia. Liquid ammonia is easy to keep and transport, but it is hard to ignite (点燃) and requires an engine redesign.

This energy transition (变革) is global, and the amount of renewable energy the world will need is “a little bit mind-blowing,” says mechanical engineer Keith Wipke at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. It’s estimated that the global demand for electricity could more than double by 2050. Fortunately, analyses suggest that renewables are up to the task. “We need to speed up the development of green energy, and it will all get used,” says Wipke.

In my ninth-grade writing class last year, I met a cowboy who saved his town, a strict father who demanded his son earn straight A’s, and a modern-day Juliet who died of heartbreak after her parents rejected the love of her young life. More than once, I found myself wondering just how my students, who’d created these people, knew their subjects so well.

But things were different for their first essay, which was about the question: “Why is writing important?” Most of the essays filled less than one page, and few contained a sentence that could be interpreted as a thesis (论点) statement. I was shocked. Then I realized that the problem was the question itself. They could have written pages on the necessity of computers, but writing, in and of itself, simply didn’t strike them as important. This would have to change.

As a new unit started, I asked everyone to write a persuasive piece on a health-related topic of their choice. This time they found the exercise much more interesting. For the next two assignments, a personal-narrative unit followed by a creative-writing workshop, I only required that the piece meet the specifications of its genre (体裁) and that it contain a thesis. The results were staggering. The students took on diverse topics and turned in stories, 10 to 20 pages each, with characters that broadened my view and touched my heart.

I walked into class believing that writing is important as a means of communication. However, my students demonstrated something more important to me. When the final bell rang in June, I walked away with a yearbook full of messages about writing’s most powerful significance — the ability to connect people, to put us in another’s skin, to teach us what it means to be human.

items.promptZh: 2018 年全球交通排放中，道路交通工具占多少？

explanation.summaryZh: 道路客运占 45.1%，道路货运占 29.4%，合计为 74.5%。
explanation.ruleZh: 图表题先识别题干对象，再合并同一大类下的分项数据。

distractors.reasonZh: 11.6% 是飞机排放占比。
45.1% 只是道路客运这一分项。
86.1% 不是图表中道路交通工具的合计值。

items.promptZh: Which mode of transport can go green comparatively easily?

explanation.summaryZh: 原文指出，有些火车已经电气化，其他火车也可以用比较简单的方式实现电动化。
explanation.ruleZh: 细节题要回到原文定位比较级或程度副词对应的句子。

evidence.quote: others can be made electric in pretty simple ways

distractors.reasonZh: 飞机是最难脱碳的领域。
卡车的绿色氢能制造成本高。
船舶需要重新设计发动机。

items.promptZh: What does Wipke suggest regarding energy transition?

explanation.summaryZh: Wipke 的建议是加快绿色能源的发展，因为未来的需求会继续增长。
explanation.ruleZh: 人物观点题优先寻找引号中的直接引语，再判断选项是否准确概括建议。

evidence.quote: We need to speed up the development of green energy

distractors.reasonZh: 原文没有建议限制燃料消耗。
原文强调发展绿色能源，而不是泛泛提高能源效率。
原文没有提出降低电价。

items.promptZh: Who are the people mentioned at the beginning of paragraph 1?

explanation.summaryZh: 段首列举的是学生创作出来的牛仔、严厉的父亲和现代版朱丽叶，都是虚构人物。
explanation.ruleZh: 人物指代题要区分故事中的角色和现实中的作者、学生。

evidence.quote: my students, who’d created these people

distractors.reasonZh: 学生是这些人物的创作者，不是题干所指的人物。
段首没有介绍学生家长。
段首人物来自学生作文，不是现实作家。

items.promptZh: Why did the students perform poorly in writing their first essay?

explanation.summaryZh: 教师后来意识到，学生表现差是因为“为什么写作重要”这个题目本身没有激发他们的兴趣。
explanation.ruleZh: 因果题要把结果句与后文的转折、解释句连起来，不能只根据前文猜测。

evidence.quote: the problem was the question itself

distractors.reasonZh: 原文没有说时间不够。
原文没有把问题归因于词汇量。
学生并非误解题目，而是认为写作本身不重要。

options.text: They were not given enough time.
They had a very limited vocabulary.
They had little interest in the topic.

items.promptZh: What does the underlined word “staggering” in paragraph 3 mean?

explanation.summaryZh: 后文列出学生写出 10 到 20 页、主题多样且打动人心的作品，因此 staggering 表示令人惊叹的。
explanation.ruleZh: 词义猜测题要用词语所在句的上下文结果和评价色彩判断。

distractors.reasonZh: 作品结果不是“混杂的”。
学生作品并非相似，而是主题多样。
上下文表达的是积极惊喜，不是令人不安。

items.promptZh: What does the author’s experience show?

explanation.summaryZh: 教师通过教学经历也发现了新的认识，说明教学过程同时也是学习过程。
explanation.ruleZh: 主旨概括题要综合首尾和转折后的核心认识，不能只看学生作品数量。

evidence.quote: my students demonstrated something more important to me

distractors.reasonZh: 文章没有讨论停滞不前。
文章重点不是知识的力量。
练习有帮助，但不是作者在结尾强调的认识。
